article.articleHeadline: Ebola in DR Congo: more than 1,700 children have died in six months.
article.articleSummary: Six months after the Ebola outbreak began in eastern DR Congo, 2,959 confirmed cases among under-18s and 1,737 deaths were reported as of Nov 4. Children are 28% of confirmed cases but 35% of fatalities; under-five children account for 14% of cases, 21% of deaths, and about 72% CFR in this group. Many children lack access to specialized care; about 80% of child deaths occur outside Ebola treatment centers, and late presentation is common; one under-five admitted dies within 24 hours. Women and girls exceed 53% of cases; among 10–17-year-olds, girls 15–17 represent two-thirds of cases and three-fifths of deaths. UNICEF and partners are expanding targeted responses in priority zones, reinforcing surveillance, early diagnosis, infection prevention, and continued access to health, nutrition, WASH, protection, and education, while urging governments and donors to bolster pediatric care and family support and protect frontline workers.

article.articleHeadline: Haut-Uele: Ebola gains ground, the governor steps up community mobilization.
article.articleSummary: As of 21 November 2026, the Haut-Uélé territory of Watsa reports 19 Ebola positive cases, including 3 deaths, prompting a high-level mobilization drive. Governor Jean Bakomito Gambu led a community-sensitization meeting in Watsa, urging all segments of the population to engage in the outbreak response, trust health teams, and observe barrier measures, while countering rumors. The gathering, attended by the provincial security committee, deputies, the Kinshasa-based Incident Manager, technical and financial partners, health officials, administrative and customary authorities, and civil society, emphasized acceptance of the disease and rapid reporting of deaths. The Provincial Health Division's response lead outlined Ebola symptoms and risk behaviors, stressing swift collaboration with responders. Participants pledged to relay prevention messages across communities to boost vigilance; authorities underscored collective responsibility to curb transmission and protect residents of Haut-Uélé.

article.articleHeadline: Bunia: 2,156 students sensitized to Ebola prevention - ACP.
article.articleSummary: As of 21 November 2026, 2,156 students at Maendeleo school in Bunia, Ituri Province, Democratic Republic of the Congo, were educated on Ebola prevention. Of these, 1,343 were girls and 813 boys. Training covered regular handwashing, recognizing Ebola symptoms, and actions for suspected cases, with emphasis on rapid reporting, countering rumors, and avoiding stigma toward affected individuals. The initiative aims to empower students as prevention ambassadors within families and communities to sustain vigilance amid the persistent Ebola outbreak in Ituri and South Kivu. The activity is part of the CREC project—risk communication, community-based surveillance, and continuity of health care in the Ebola response—implemented by the Observatoire des droits humains with UNICEF funding.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola in Ituri: Local Organizations Urged to Strengthen Ebola Prevention - ACP.
article.articleSummary: As of 21 November 2026, Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) outbreak in Ituri Province, Democratic Republic of Congo, specifically in Djugu's Bahema Nord chiefdom, with confirmed cases reported at Drodro General Referral Hospital. Local civil society organizations are urged to intensify community awareness campaigns in affected areas to promote Ebola prevention and protect households. Charité Banza, president of the Bahema Nord civil society umbrella, notes that humanitarian organizations usually operate on time-bound projects and depart, potentially leaving communities without sustained sensitization and support. He calls for capacity-building of competent local groups to maintain prevention activities, address gender-based violence, and resolve land and parcel disputes. Partners should identify and train local structures to ensure post-departure continuity. Strengthened collaboration between humanitarian actors and local organizations could reinforce community prevention mechanisms and sustain Ebola response.

article.articleHeadline: News | Ebola: 67 healthcare workers have died, Professor Éric Mafuta insists on early detection of epidemics
article.articleSummary: During the Democratic Republic of Congo's 17th Ebola outbreak, frontline clinicians are emphasized as critical alerting agents in the response. Professor Éric Mafuta, director of the School of Public Health at the University of Kinshasa (UNIKIN), told a Médecins Promotion 2003 conference series that clinicians must recognize events or clinical pictures signaling an epidemic and must notify authorities promptly. Africa CDC data reported as of early November 2026 show 427 healthcare workers infected since the outbreak was declared on 15 May 2026, with 67 deaths among them. Mafuta links the toll to lapses in infection prevention and control, urging clinicians to listen to their communities and maintain precautions in practice. The report underscores ongoing Ebola transmission in the DRC and the essential role of early detection and surveillance in mitigating casualties.

article.articleHeadline: Silver nanoparticles proved effective against Aedes aegypti
article.articleSummary: Green-synthesized silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) show high efficacy against Aedes aegypti larvae and schistosome cercariae in water. In a Butantan Institute study led by Luiz Gustavo Ribeiro and Ana Olivia de Souza, AgNPs produced via fungal extracts from Aspergillus tubingensis (isolated from a mangrove) kill Schistosoma cercariae at low concentrations within two hours, preventing transmission from contaminated rivers and lakes. The same nanoparticles blocked the progression of Aedes aegypti larvae to adults 48 hours after application, reducing dengue, Zika, and chikungunya risk. Unlike chemical molluscicides, the approach does not kill snails, fish, or microcrustaceans in tested conditions, due to gradual release. Patented by INPI in July 2026, the technology is ready for industrial scaling and licensing. Dengue affects up to 400 million annually (WHO); Brazil logged over 1 million cases in 2025 and 6.6 million in 2024, while schistosomiasis affects over 200 million globally and remains endemic in parts of Brazil.

article.articleHeadline: Dengue: a mother who lost her daughter and a patient who survived tell their stories.
article.articleSummary: Dengue in the Brazilian Federal District (Distrito Federal, DF) is highlighted on National Dengue Combat Day (Nov 21, 2026) with two stark experiences. DF reported a 54% drop in probable dengue cases through epidemiological week 45 (by Nov 16, 2026): 4,540 cases this year vs 9,904 in 2025, and notifications declined from 21,544 to 13,060. In 2023, Camila Isaac, 40, lost her seven-year-old daughter Pietra Isaac de Carvalho to dengue hemorrhagic fever; the case is in court seeking accountability from a physician after an initial misdiagnosis and delayed hospitalization. Conversely, 61-year-old Alex Coelho Papeira of Ponte Alta survived dengue hemorrhagic fever in 2023, requiring ICU care and later recovery, attributing his illness to a neighbor’s contaminated pool and warning against self-medication. Dengue is transmitted by Aedes aegypti; clinicians note the risk window around days 3–7 after fever onset, while El Niño may influence transmission but is not the sole cause.

article.articleHeadline: Can a bat transmit rabies? What to do after possible exposure.
article.articleSummary: Rabies exposure from bats in Curitiba, Brazil, requires immediate medical evaluation for any bite, scratch, or direct contact. Guidance from the city emphasizes washing the wound with soap and water before presenting to a health unit, where clinicians determine the appropriate treatment. Do not touch or handle the bat; isolate it and call 156 to arrange removal and laboratory testing by the Unidade de Vigilância de Zoonoses (UVZ). Contact near a child or in a bedroom warrants evaluation even without visible wounds. If dogs or cats contact a bat, take them to a veterinarian; isolate the bat if present and request removal. Vaccination against rabies is stressed, with UVZ offering free vaccination at Rua Lodovico Kaminski 1,381, CIC, Curitiba. Rabies is a Lyssavirus infection affecting the CNS, transmitted mainly by bat saliva via bites or saliva contacting wounds and mucous membranes; early treatment saves lives.

article.articleHeadline: Belém and Santarém account for nearly 60% of dengue deaths in Pará.
article.articleSummary: Pará reports 8,749 confirmed dengue cases through October 2026, with 17 deaths in the period. Belém and Santarém accounted for 10 deaths and 2,462 cases; Santarém had 1,101 cases, Belém 1,361. Castanhal, Conceição do Araguaia, and Mãe do Rio show high incidence (683, 364, 349) with no deaths. About 11,100 probable dengue cases in 2026 in Pará, down 43.6% from 2024; Brazil had 485,400 probable cases by October 2026, down 92.5% from the previous year. Federal actions include expanding larvicide dissemination stations, training around 100 Belém professionals (Nov 5), and donating 86 BRI-Aedes devices. Belém launched a citywide campaign (Nov 12–29) with 80 agents; dengue vaccination for ages 10–14 continues nationwide (17.6 million doses distributed since 2024; 10.9 million administered).

article.articleHeadline: One invisible toll of war is worsening drug-resistant TB crisis
article.articleSummary: War and humanitarian emergencies fuel the burden of drug-resistant tuberculosis (DR-TB) by destroying health services and driving displacement. In 2024, nearly 300 million people needed humanitarian aid, with 83.4 million internally displaced (73.5 million from conflict/violence). Prolonged conflicts in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Lebanon, Palestine, Sudan, Ukraine, and ongoing crises in Afghanistan, Colombia, Syria and Yemen create poverty, malnutrition, overcrowding and disrupted diagnosis and treatment, increasing TB transmission and the emergence of drug resistance. A 2026 BMJ Global Health scoping review co-authored by Dr Ignacio Monedero Recuero found fewer than 20% of estimated DR-TB cases are notified in complex emergencies, leaving many undiagnosed. Globally, only 38% of estimated DR-TB cases were notified and treated in 2025 per the WHO Global TB Report 2026. The urgency: identify all DR-TB cases and link them to treatment and support; war-affected settings must be prioritized in the TB response, a theme at the Stop TB Partnership session during the 55th Union World Conference in Rio de Janeiro.

Campo Grande confirmed a case at Escola Municipal de Educação Infantil Jasmim Ibrahim Bacha in Nova Lima; the school was cleaned on 18 November and resumed on 19 November, while three additional suspected cases are being investigated. The Ministry notes scabies is not a public health emergency in Brazil but requires preventive measures, including treating close contacts, washing shared items in hot water, and avoiding sharing personal items. Transmission is mainly via prolonged skin-to-skin contact; investigations are ongoing.

article.articleHeadline: El Niño could reverse the 93% drop in dengue cases in Paraná.
article.articleSummary: As of the 44th epidemiological week of 2026, Paraná, Brazil reports 6,380 dengue cases, a 93% drop from the same period in 2025, with deaths down from 114 to 6 (~95% reduction). The Aedes aegypti vector remains the key threat; higher temperatures, humidity, and heavy rains associated with El Niño could boost mosquito reproduction and transmission of dengue, Zika, and chikungunya, potentially reversing gains. Nationally, Fiocruz projects about 866,000 probable dengue cases in 2027 under a strong El Niño, with an uncertainty range of roughly 560,000 to 1.6 million, and about 80% confidence the final total falls within that band. In Paraná, vigilance must continue to eliminate standing water to prevent new breeding sites, since outbreaks depend on virus circulation, population susceptibility, and surveillance quality. El Niño could contribute but is not the sole driver; prior surges occurred during 2023–2024.

article.articleHeadline: Century of Newcastle Disease Virus Research Traces Evolution and Vaccine
article.articleSummary: Newcastle disease virus (NDV) is a notifiable avian pathogen (Paramyxoviridae, Avulavirinae, Orthoavulavirus javaense) with economic impact from high flock mortality, reduced egg production, and trade embargoes. A centennial retrospective traces its identification in 1926 after outbreaks in Java, Indonesia and Newcastle-upon-Tyne, England. NDV comprises Class II genotypes and a Class I lineage; genomes are about 15.2 kb. The virion carries HN and F glycoproteins; V and W proteins arise via translational frameshifts and antagonize host interferon signaling (STAT1, MDA5). Infection starts with HN binding sialic acids and a pH-independent F protein fusion after proteolytic cleavage. Pathotypes span viscerotropic velogenic (up to 100% mortality in naive birds within 3–9 days), neurotropic velogenic, and mesogenic forms. US eradication efforts (1971–73, 2002–03) depopulated millions of birds and cost hundreds of millions. Since the 1920s, NDV has caused at least four major panzootics with persistent endemicity in wildlife and poultry.

article.articleHeadline: Video | Rethink Your Understanding: Even if mosquitoes can't be eliminated, dengue fever can be prevented—new ways to control mosquitoes!
article.articleSummary: Dengue fever and Zika, transmitted by mosquitoes, affect nearly 400 million people annually worldwide. Shenzhen-based researchers propose two green, non-lethal strategies to curb transmission in Asia-Pacific. First, introduce a natural gut bacterium, GD01, into wild mosquitoes; field deployment in Shenzhen’s Guangming District parks and residential areas since June 2026 shows over 80% gut colonization, aiming to block viruses inside mosquitoes and prevent spread. Plans include testing in Malaysia and Indonesia. Second, disable the mosquitoes’ ability to locate humans by targeting the odor-sensing pocket in their olfactory system, potentially using cryo-EM insights to develop blocking agents; this approach is still at the basic-research stage. The goal is environmental-ecological intervention toward a “green, long-acting” solution and a disease-transmission icepoint region, aligning with APAC dengue control Roadmap.

article.articleHeadline: Pulmonary Tuberculosis Patients Show Altered Gut Viral Diversity and Phage
article.articleSummary: Pulmonary tuberculosis in a China-based cohort (46 patients vs 31 healthy controls) shows altered gut virome composition. TB patients exhibit significantly reduced gut viral alpha-diversity, with a modest overall compositional shift; multivariate dispersion differed between groups. Viruses enriched in healthy controls belonged to Fervensviridae and Phycodnaviridae, while TB-enriched OTUs were dominated by Microviridae and Winoviridae. TB-associated viruses more frequently linked to Bacteroides and Parabacteroides; control-associated viruses linked to butyrate-producing Gemmiger, Lachnospira, and Roseburia. Cross-kingdom networks revealed 1,182 significant bacterium–virus co-abundance relationships in TB vs 922 in controls, with distinct topology. Functionally, the LexA repressor (KEGG K01356) was more prevalent among TB-associated viral OTUs, suggesting stress-response roles. Diagnostic models: virus-only AUC 91.5% (discovery); external 89.4%; bacteria-only 90.6% (discovery) and 95.0% external; combined ~89.5% external. Conclusion: gut virome alterations and phage–host dynamics characterize pulmonary TB.

article.articleHeadline: qPCR Outperformed Serological Tests in Screening Asymptomatic Dogs for
article.articleSummary: Yangquan City, Shanxi Province, China, hosted a field comparison of four diagnostic assays for Leishmania infection in 175 asymptomatic dogs from an endemic area. article.articleHeadline: It's too dirty! Qingtian residents, check yourselves now! Many people have been using it recently; some have 'a fever of 40°C and a lung infection' — Qingtian Net.
article.articleSummary: Legionella pneumonia linked to unclean air-conditioning systems in Xi’an, Shaanxi Province, China. article.articleHeadline: Standard Risk Model Outperforms Expanded Framework in Predicting COVID-19
article.articleSummary: In Wuhan, China, during the early COVID-19 outbreak, 822 local adults (March 3–5, 2020) completed an online survey testing PRISM against an expanded PRISM that added source beliefs, past information seeking, and outcome expectancies. The original five-factor, 21-indicator PRISM fit the data well, with perceived knowledge positively linked to knowledge insufficiency; however, perceived behavioral control and affective risk responses did not directly predict knowledge insufficiency, and attitudes toward seeking did not directly relate to seeking intention. The expanded model, comprising nine factors and 44 indicators, yielded poorer fit metrics, and after adding structural paths, remained inferior. It explained about 30 percent of the variance in information-seeking intentions, indicating diminished predictive power compared with the original framework. Conclusion: for predicting public COVID-19 risk information seeking in this Wuhan sample, the standard PRISM outperforms the expanded framework.

article.articleHeadline: Norovirus hard to eradicate? Doctors warn against mopping up vomit; four proper steps for whole-house disinfection
article.articleSummary: Norovirus outbreaks peak in autumn–winter. This virus persists over two weeks on hard and soft surfaces. Viral shedding may continue for two weeks or more after symptoms end, so those who recover should avoid food preparation for others at least 48 hours. Do not mop vomit; use disposable towels to prevent aerosol spread. Four-step cleanup: wear disposable gloves and a surgical mask; blot from edge to center; seal contaminated waste in bags; disinfect and ventilate. Bleach solutions: general surfaces 1:99; heavily contaminated areas 1:49; CDC says contact time 5 minutes; CHP 15–30 minutes. Launder contaminated textiles by soaking in 1:49 for 30 minutes, wash at ≥60°C, and dry on high heat; steam-clean if not washable. After cleaning, soak reusable tools in 1:49 for 30 minutes. Handwash with running water for 20 seconds; avoid alcohol sanitizers. Cleveland Clinic physician Matthew Goldman emphasizes hygiene, bleach disinfection, and not handling food during illness.

article.articleHeadline: Fifty Paces Outside the Camp: Latrines, Fetching Water, and the Plague in the Army
article.articleSummary: Historical military campaigns link sanitation to disease outcomes. Sunzi’s guidance to station camps on high, dry ground away from dampness foreshadows the idea that disease follows environment, not just enemy action, with military “no hundred diseases” only achievable by controlling the camp’s soil and water. The Red Cliffs episode (208 CE) is the classic example: Cao Cao’s forces faced a major epidemic after moving into new water and soils, undermining battle readiness; pre-battle warnings by Zhou Yu cautioned that Central Plains troops unfamiliar with local water and land would contract disease. Thus, plague there stemmed from transferring troops into unfamiliar ecologies, not merely camp hygiene. In Ming–Qing times, cleanliness routines persisted, yet epidemics returned (notably in Jiangnan around 1862–63). The text stresses a boundary: camp sanitation protects the interior but cannot guard against external environmental pathogens. It also notes weapon logistics—bow and crossbow materials—whose moisture sensitivity and seasonal production reveal how epidemics and wear simultaneously erode military capacity.

article.articleHeadline: Changing seasonality and trends of other infectious diarrhea and norovirus across the pandemic era in Shenzhen China
article.articleSummary: OID (other infectious diarrhea) and norovirus trends in Shenzhen, China, from 1 Jan 2013 to 31 Jul 2025 analyzed across pre-, during-, and post-COVID-19 periods. The study uses 578,222 OID reports plus monthly norovirus GI-positive, GII-positive, and GI+GII-positive series. In a climate-adjusted ARMA(2,0) model, OID reports fell 48.1% in Feb 2020 and then rose 2.15% per month, with a slope-change of 1.13% per month (CI included zero). A Jan 2022 sensitivity model suggested a positive post-break trend of 3.28% per month, but its slope-change also included zero. A three-segment model found no additional acceleration in Jan 2022 relative to 2020–2021. Meteorological covariates (temperature, relative humidity, wet-day frequency) did not explain the later positive trend. Conclusion: changing surveillance dynamics during the COVID-19 era, not a unique or causal 2022 acceleration, drive observed patterns in Shenzhen.

article.articleHeadline: Respiratory Compartments in Chickens Direct Distinct Pathways of H9N2 Avian
article.articleSummary: H9N2 avian influenza viruses circulating in domestic poultry show tissue-specific evolution in chickens: upper respiratory tract selects mutations increasing human-type α2,6 sialic acid receptor affinity, while lower respiratory tissues favor substitutions enabling antibody escape. Since 2010, two lineages dominate: B (77% of HA sequences in Asia) and G (15% across Africa and the Middle East), with ~15–20% divergence from ancestral strains. The HA bears 71 diversity hotspots, eight hypervariable sites (e.g., 160, 190), and historical isolates shifted from dual receptor usage before 2002 to human-like binding after 2005. A G57-lineage HA from A/chicken/Beijing/16/2013 was used to build a 20,496-mutant library (8,935 substitutions). In MDCK cells and eggs it replicated; in BALB/c mice it caused respiratory-limited infection with full survival. In chickens with naive, heterologous-vaccinated, homologous-vaccinated, or convalescent immunity, naive shed most; convalescents the least; homologous vaccination and prior infection blocked transmission, while heterologous reduced shedding but did not fully stop transmission. Sequencing showed bottlenecks and that pre-existing immunity constrains diversity.

article.articleHeadline: Enhanced 3D ResNet Model Classifies Active Pulmonary Tuberculosis on Chest
article.articleSummary: Active versus inactive pulmonary tuberculosis differentiation on chest CT achieved with 3D MSGC-ResNet50, a deep-learning classifier built from 3D ResUNet lung segmentation. Retrospective data from 500 patients at Guiyang Public Health Treatment Center, Guiyang City, Guizhou Province (250 active TB, 250 inactive TB) yielded internal metrics: precision 94.87%, recall 91.60%, F1-score 93.19%, AUC 96.68%, with the MSGC-ResNet50 outperforming baseline 3D ResNet50 by about 3–5 percentage points across metrics. External validation on 40 cases from a separate hospital achieved 90.00% accuracy (36 correct, 4 misclassified), indicating preliminary cross-institutional generalizability. The pipeline segments lung parenchyma via 3D ResUNet, then classifies with MSGC enhancements—multi-scale attention and grouped convolution with channel shuffle—to better capture lesion features. The approach aims to assist clinicians in timely TB management and transmission prevention, leveraging cross-institutional data for broader applicability.

article.articleHeadline: TimeMixer Model Reduced Nine-Month Tuberculosis Forecasting Errors in
article.articleSummary: TB forecasting in Kashgar Prefecture, Xinjiang, China, using monthly reported pulmonary TB incidence across twelve counties (2011–2025) with holdout test Jan–Sep 2025. Evaluated models include naive persistence, seasonal naive, SARIMA, iTransformer, TimeMixer, and BiRNN across 3-, 6-, and 9-month horizons. For 3 months, naive persistence yields MAE 2.193 per 100,000; TimeMixer performs worse at 4.804. For 6 months, naive persistence MAE is 3.217, again outperforming TimeMixer. At 9 months, TimeMixer shows strongest accuracy (RMSE 15.960 per 100,000; MAE 6.580 per 100,000; R^2=0.039) vs naive persistence MAE 7.430. Historical mean incidence (2016–2020) is 32.05 per 100,000; seasonal strength is low (0.090). Three 2025 outliers were flagged; excluding them lowers errors but leaves the ranking unchanged. Multimodel forecasts offer supplementary surveillance value; resource decisions should rely on broader epidemiological assessments, with transferability needing further evaluation.

article.articleHeadline: Human Bocavirus Peaked in Young Children Across Eastern China Hospitals
article.articleSummary: In eastern China, 12,630 hospitalized children with acute respiratory infections were tested from January 2025 to March 2026 using a 13-target multiplex RT-PCR panel (SureX 13 Respiratory Pathogen Multiplex Kit, Ningbo Health Gene Technologies). Human bocavirus (HBoV) was detected in 3.2% overall, with no sex difference (p=0.99) but higher positivity in ages 1–3 years (7.7%). Co-infections occurred frequently, with human rhinovirus, respiratory syncytial virus, and human parainfluenza viruses most common alongside HBoV. Mono-infections numbered 230; double-infections 154; triple-infections 26. Hospital length of stay did not differ significantly by co-infection pattern or infection multiplicity (mono 5.9 days; double 6.1; triple 6.7; p=0.700), though Mycoplasma pneumoniae co-infection lengthened stays (8.3 days) and Chlamydia co-infection shortened them (4.0 days; p=0.279). Clinical scores followed similar non-significant trends. A SARIMA model forecasts HBoV peaks in August–September 2026 to guide seasonal resource planning.

The cow, bitten while grazing, showed rabies symptoms and died around midnight; owner Nakul Patel buried the animal. Several villagers had consumed the cow’s milk and dairy products. Health officials emphasised there is no established evidence that rabies is transmitted through milk, curd, or buttermilk. Dr Indu Rajput, in-charge of Chargawan PHC, and CMHO Dr Naveen Kothari advised residents not to panic and to seek immediate medical attention after an animal bite or exposure to an animal’s saliva.

article.articleHeadline: As the cold sets in, seasonal infections strike children, with pneumonia also posing a risk.
article.articleSummary: As of 21 November 2026, the pediatric department at Ranchi's Rajendra Institute of Medical Sciences (RIMS) reports a surge in seasonal respiratory infections among infants and young children as temperatures drop. About 20–25 children visit daily with respiratory infections and other seasonal illnesses, up from 15–20 last year. Infants aged 3–7 months are presenting upper respiratory infections with wheezing, breathing difficulty, high fever, and sometimes red eyes and diarrhea. In 2–5-year-olds, ear pain and ear discharge are increasingly reported. Infections can spread to lower airways, raising pneumonia risk, with breathing trouble, wheeze and high fever as key signs. Sudden temperature changes and cold exposure are identified as risk factors. Parents are advised to monitor symptoms closely and seek medical advice; limit exposure to infected individuals and maintain hygiene.

article.articleHeadline: Is Your Body Ready For Winter? Common Infections Adults Over 50 Should Know About
article.articleSummary: Winter increases exposure to infections such as influenza and other respiratory illnesses. In adults over 50, immunosenescence heightens susceptibility to infections like influenza and pneumococcal pneumonia, with those over 50 nearly six times more likely to contract pneumococcal pneumonia than younger adults. Shingles (varicella zoster) also warrants attention in this age group, as it can cause severe pain and long-term complications such as postherpetic neuralgia beyond a rash. In India, Streptococcus pneumoniae is among the leading causes of community-acquired pneumonia. Preventive health for adults over 50 should combine lifestyle measures (diet, exercise, hand hygiene, avoiding smoking), management of chronic conditions, and vaccination. Seek medical advice for preventive vaccination and personalized risk reduction. The piece emphasizes that protection is not only about treatment after illness but reducing risk through proactive measures during winter.

article.articleHeadline: Malaria Cases And Deaths Fall 80% In India Over 10 Years, But Climate Change Could Reverse Gains
article.articleSummary: Malaria in India declined nearly 80% in cases and deaths from 2015 to 2025, aided by improved diagnosis, treatment, vector-control campaigns, and public awareness. The burden shift is evident as districts with high malaria reduced from 155 to 33; between 2022 and 2025, as many as 160 districts reported no locally transmitted malaria. India targets malaria elimination by 2030, but climate change—rising temperatures, altered rainfall, and rapid urbanisation—could create favorable mosquito breeding conditions and threaten gains. Insecticide resistance may further hamper control efforts. Ongoing emphasis on early diagnosis, appropriate treatment, mosquito-control, surveillance, and community participation remains essential. Preventive actions include avoiding stagnant water, covering water containers, sleeping under mosquito nets, and seeking timely medical testing for fever rather than self-medication.

article.articleSummary: Rabies prevention in Keralam centers on a comprehensive policy and action plan to achieve a rabies-free status by 2030, announced during a One Health seminar. The seminar, held on November 21, featured the inaugural address by Kozhikode deputy mayor S. Jayasree, with IMA State president P. Gopikumar and IVA State general secretary A. Irshad among speakers. article.articleHeadline: Hostels face scrutiny after students report worms in food
article.articleSummary: Odisha's college and university hostels are under scrutiny after worms were found in meals, starting with Nagabali Girls' Hostel at Maa Manikeswari University in Bhawanipatna. Students protested after worms appeared in the mess on Friday; the university denies the allegations and promises an assessment. The case follows earlier incidents this year: Ravenshaw University in Cuttack saw Mahanadi Girls' Hostel students protest Oct 4 over worms; BPUT in Rourkela faced a meal boycott on Oct 11 after a video showing a worker kneading dough with feet; Utkal University reported a dead frog in a soybean dish at Girls' Hostel No. 7 in early Nov amid a Hepatitis A scare. Authorities cite the Food Safety and Standards Act 2006 (FSSAI registrations/licences) and UGC hygiene norms; officials say compliance is uneven and some blame deliberate contamination by students, while many institutions follow norms.

article.articleHeadline: Respiratory infections empty classrooms benches, fill Hospital beds
article.articleSummary: As of 21 November 2026, Chennai hospitals report respiratory infections driving full wards and ICUs, keeping children home from school. Infants under one year are most affected by respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), with severe RSV cases requiring pediatric ICU care; several infants are very ill. Older children in ICUs test positive for influenza A (H1N1) or influenza B; many cases feature runny nose, itchy throat, high fever, cough. While most outpatient cases are viral infections and influenza, dengue also appears among pediatric patients. A preventive option against severe RSV is nirsevimab, given within birth or before the first RSV season; a single dose lasts at least five months and costs ₹30,000-₹40,000. Roughly the price of one day in intensive care. Household transmission is common; testing is prioritized for severely ill or those with comorbidities. Vaccination reduces severity; some high-risk children may need a second dose before the next RSV season.

article.articleHeadline: ASF strikes 4 Quezon villages; hog raisers urged to stay vigilant
article.articleSummary: African Swine Fever strikes four barangays in Macalelon, Quezon (Mabini Ibaba, Amontay, Candangal, Pinagbayanan). Lab results confirmed on Nov 11. ASF is a highly contagious viral disease affecting domestic and wild pigs; it does not affect humans, and pork from infected animals is not safe for consumption. Immediate response by the Municipal Agriculture Office includes surveillance and testing, plus depopulation or controlled culling of affected pigs in the identified barangays. Biosecurity measures are intensified in barangays with no reported cases. Hog raisers are urged to monitor for weakness, loss of appetite, fever, skin redness, or other symptoms, and to avoid transporting pigs without permits; pigpens should be kept clean and secured, with unauthorized persons and vehicles blocked. The Department of Agriculture posts vaccination programs and stricter livestock-movement controls, with ASF checkpoints to inspect vehicles and health certificates, plus restrictions on traders, breeders, and shipments of frozen pork. At least four additional ASF vaccines are eyed by next year (2027). Published 2026-11-21.

article.articleHeadline: Cholera cases in the Philippines rise 69% in two weeks; Health Department urges safeguarding of drinking water and food safety.
article.articleSummary: Cholera cases in the Philippines rose 69% in two weeks; from Oct 11–24, 27 cases, up from 16, with as of Nov 7 cumulative 551 cases and a case fatality rate of 2.18%. Two regions are under heightened monitoring for cholera. Typhoid fever reached 1,141 cases (up 4% from the prior two weeks), totaling 16,432 cases by Nov 7, CFR 0.30%. Ten regions, 15 provinces and highly urbanized cities are monitored due to sustained increases in typhoid. Acute hemorrhagic diarrhea this year Jan 4–Nov 7 totals 8,601 cases (down 25% YoY). Influenza-like illness: 150,187 cases (down 15%). Dengue: 254,090 cases (down 9%). El Niño could affect safe drinking water and mosquito breeding. Public guidance urges safe water, thorough cooking of food, hygiene; seek care for persistent fever, severe abdominal pain, repeated vomiting, bloody stools, or marked fatigue; eliminate standing water to reduce dengue risk.

article.articleHeadline: Sullana Specialty Hospital Consolidates a High Recovery Rate Among Dengue Patients.
article.articleSummary: Peru's Sullana Specialty Hospital (MINSA) reports a high dengue recovery rate amid the Aedes aegypti–driven outbreak. Since the contingency began, 777 dengue patients have been discharged from specialized care. Official data show 1,087 emergency consultations for suspected dengue, with 641 laboratory-confirmed cases, 136 probable, and 310 discarded; four deaths occurred from severe complications. In the Santa Rosa site, the Clinical Surveillance Unit (UVICLIN) achieved 582 discharges of 588 treated (98.9% effectiveness). Overall, 321 additional discharges occurred in hospitalization and observation services, and 171 children recovered in the pediatric ward. Patients without alarm signs at triage were referred back to their local health centers for ambulatory management. Authorities urge reinforced vector-control measures: eliminate mosquito breeding sites, use repellent, and seek immediate care for high fever, severe abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, or bleeding, avoiding self-medication.

article.articleHeadline: Boy with viral gastroenteritis.
article.articleSummary: In Hanoi, a 21‑month‑old boy with viral gastroenteritis presented with vomiting, abdominal distension, and 3–4 loose stools daily. Leukocytosis and elevated CRP were noted; glucose, electrolytes, and calcium were normal. Ultrasound showed mesenteric lymphadenopathy and small free fluid in the right iliac fossa. No focal neurological signs; meningitis was excluded. Brain MRI found bilateral occipital subcortical white‑matter abnormalities, interpreted as post‑ictal. Rotavirus, Norovirus, and Adenovirus were negative. Diagnosed with a seizure after acute viral gastroenteritis of unknown etiology, with concurrent acute upper respiratory infection. Treatment included seizure control, rehydration and electrolyte management, and symptomatic GI/respiratory care, plus nasal irrigation with 0.9% saline. After 3 days, vomiting stopped, seizures did not recur, and the child was discharged. Prevention: handwashing, safe food/water, Rotavirus vaccination.

article.articleHeadline: Dak Lak: Holding department heads accountable for dengue fever prevention and control
article.articleSummary: Dengue fever in Dak Lak Province, Vietnam, has reached 13,074 new cases and 3 deaths through November 20, 2026, with 81 active outbreaks. The surge is driven by alternating rain and sun and water-filled containers that sustain Aedes mosquito breeding; several localities show gaps in eradication efforts and surveillance. In response, Vice Chairman Ho Thi Nguyen Thao issued a directive to strengthen prevention and control, mandating that all agencies and local governments prioritize dengue, implement the four-at-site principle, and assign responsibility to communes and hamlets. The Department of Health leads weekly risk assessments, enhances epidemiological and vector surveillance, and oversees outbreak investigation, larviciding, insecticide spraying, and stockpiles of chemicals and equipment. Local centers will bolster staffing and coordinate with authorities to prevent healthcare overload. Very high-risk areas include Buon Ma Thuot wards, and localities such as Tan An, Tan Lap, Ea Kao, Krong Pac, Tan Tien, Ea Tul, Cu M’Gar, Ea Drong, and Hoa Phu.

article.articleHeadline: Hanoi tightens monkeypox prevention and control measures
article.articleSummary: Hanoi tightens monkeypox prevention and control amid risk of importation via international travel. Hanoi CDC is coordinating with Noi Bai International Airport and related agencies to strengthen airport surveillance to promptly identify suspected cases, especially from countries with ongoing transmission. The agency also works with district health posts to monitor gynecology, dermatology, ARV, and methadone clinics for suspected cases and with the National Institute of Hygiene and Epidemiology and the National Hospital for Tropical Diseases to obtain samples for confirmation. Public-information campaigns are intensified to raise awareness per Ministry of Health guidance, and health facilities are urged to ensure medicines, supplies, staff, and funding for prompt treatment. Citizens should self-isolate if symptoms appear and seek medical testing; travelers from affected areas should declare to health authorities. Transmission occurs animal-to-human and human-to-human via direct contact with lesions, body fluids, droplets, contaminated objects, mother-to-child, and sexual contact. Symptoms include fever, headache, muscle pains, lymphadenopathy, fatigue, and vesicular rash; disease usually resolves in 2–3 weeks and is more severe in children, pregnant women, and immunocompromised individuals.

article.articleHeadline: Ha Tinh Province strengthens prevention and control of African swine fever.
article.articleSummary: African swine fever (ASF) in Ha Tinh Province, Vietnam, remains a major concern as of 22 November 2026. The disease has spread to 45 hamlets across 19 communes/wards, affecting over 600 pigs that are currently infected, dead, or culled. In Thiên Cầm commune, ASF is largely controlled in November with only 2 households infected, down from October; since 20 October, Đồng Lộc commune reported re-emergence in 4 hamlets affecting 9 households. The province faces ongoing risk due to seasonal movement of pigs and potential cross-border incursions from Laos, where ASF activity could enter via unregulated trade and border crossings. Authorities emphasize strict biosecurity, surveillance, market checks, and rapid reporting; directives issued on 23 Oct (MARD Document 12237/BNNMT-CNTY) and 29 Oct (11226/UBND-NL5) bolster control. Mitraco (about 6,500 sows and ~150,000 pigs/year) and other farms reinforce hygiene and disinfection to maintain meat supply for year-end and Tet 2027, and farmers are urged to source clean stock, vaccinate fully, and report signs promptly.

article.articleHeadline: Antiviral activity of Clinacanthus siamensis Bremek ethanolic extract against dengue virus serotype 2 infection
article.articleSummary: Dengue virus serotype 2 (DENV-2) infection remains without a specific antiviral therapy, with vaccines showing variable efficacy. An ethanolic extract of Thai medicinal herb Clinacanthus siamensis demonstrated potent anti-DENV activity in vitro, yielding an IC50 of 19.32 µg/mL. Time-of-addition experiments revealed the greatest inhibition under pre-treatment conditions, with viral protein levels reduced to 92.79±7.74%, 60.30±9.79%, and 12.52±10.18% at 15.625, 31.25, and 62.5 µg/mL, respectively, indicating action at early infection stages. Virus-binding assays showed pretreatment of virions with the extract impaired their ability to bind host cells, suggesting a direct effect on viral particles. LC-MS/MS identified two antiviral constituents, isoferulic acid and luteolin, that may contribute to the effect. Overall, Clinacanthus siamensis exhibits anti-DENV activity by reducing infectivity early and warrants further development as an affordable therapeutic candidate against DENV infection.

article.articleHeadline: Thai Hospital Study Identifies Shifting Carbapenem Resistance and
article.articleSummary: Three-year surveillance at Suddhavej Hospital, Mahasarakham University, in northeastern Thailand analyzed 2,190 Enterobacterales isolates from 4,147 records (1,638 deduplicated from 1,320 patients) to assess carbapenem resistance (2023–2025). Urinary specimens dominated (54.4% in 2023 to 65.3% in 2025). Escherichia coli rose from 48.7% to 57.1% of isolates; Klebsiella pneumoniae fell from 33.9% to 23.1%. Carbapenem resistance among recovered isolates declined from 8.4% (2023) to 6.3% (2024) to 2.7% (2025); overall carbapenem nonsusceptibility fell from 12.6% to 5.4%. Cefotaxime resistance remained stable (27.7–30.3%). In 2025, ertapenem-nonsusceptible isolates numbered 25, with nine retaining susceptibility to both meropenem and imipenem (ertapenem-discordant). These nine included Klebsiella pneumoniae, Escherichia coli, Enterobacter cloacae complex, Citrobacter koseri from urine (5), respiratory (2), deep tissue (1), bloodstream (1). Authors note confirmatory carbapenemase testing/genomic sequencing is required to elucidate resistance mechanisms.

article.articleHeadline: Zambia : Chilanga Acting DC Calls For Combined Efforts In Cholera Fight
article.articleSummary: Chilanga district, Zambia, has recorded 146 cholera cases since August, with two deaths (one in the community and one at a health facility). On 19 November 2026, there were 5 new admissions and 4 discharges; 3 patients remain admitted in health facilities. The highest case numbers are in Kasupe and Chilanga wards. Four wards report relatively high locally acquired cases, indicating ongoing community transmission: Mt Makulu Ward (23), Nyemba Ward (16), New Farms Ward (13), and Mondegwa Ward (10). Other wards have smaller counts: Kalundu (1), Nakachenje (1), Chilongolo (3), Namalombwe (3), and Mwembeshi (4). District officials plan to strengthen surveillance and community-level interventions and will closely monitor the situation. Acting District Commissioner Maureen Chilende urged concerted efforts from all stakeholders to fight the disease, stressing the importance of healthy people for production and continued cholera response.

triage.headline_ja: ザンビア：チランガ副地区長がコレラ対策への協力を呼びかけ
triage.triage_reason: ザンビア・チランガ地区で進行中のコレラアウトブレイク（146例、死亡2名、地域内伝播継続）の定期経過報告であり、新規の重大進展は見られないため続報を注視する。
triage.notes: 既存のコレラアウトブレイク（2026年8月以降）の地区レベル定期報告。複数ワードで地域内伝播が継続しており、監視強化が必要だが国際的拡大や渡航制限の兆候は記事内に記載なし。
